questions: Should the function treat names as case-sensitive? For example, should 'John' and 'john' be considered the same name?
What should happen if a name contains square brackets (e.g., 'John [Smith]')? Does the regex extract only the part before the first bracket?
How should whitespace be handled? Should leading/trailing spaces be stripped, and should multiple spaces within a name be collapsed?
If there are no names (empty result), should the returned pandas Series be empty or None?
Should the bar chart axes have specific labels (x-axis, y-axis) beyond the title 'Name Frequencies'?
What if the text contains nested brackets (e.g., 'John [addr [inner]]')? Does the regex handle non-greedy matching correctly?
Should the skewness and kurtosis be computed using bias correction (Fisher's definition) or not? scipy.stats.kurtosis defaults to Fisher's.
If there is only one unique name (frequency count of 1), skewness and kurtosis may be undefined (nan). Should they be set to None, 0, or left as nan?
